text: Working the one queued task: writing the plan for the Files-tab ticket. Reading the code behind the tab now.
Still reading: now checking how the files list is fetched and what git the branches provider can already answer, then I'll write the plan.

I wrote the plan for the Files-tab ticket, the only task on the queue. The queue is now empty. The plan is saved on `agent-data` as `tickets/2026-09-21_files-tab-after-checkout.plan.md`, with Effort 4 and Uncertainty 3. I released my claim and marked the queue entry done. A plan opens no pull request, so none was opened. No code was changed, so nothing was built or tested.

The main points of the plan:
- **The cause:** the Files tab looks up the run's checkout, and once that checkout is reclaimed it quietly shows the project root instead. That's why a finished run looks as if it changed nothing. It also marks only uncommitted changes, so committed work goes unmarked even while the checkout still exists.
- **The fix:** a new read, `onAgentTree`, returns the file list and the changes together. It tries three sources in order: the checkout, then the run's branch (local, then the copy on origin), then the merge commit named by the run's recorded pull request. When none is left, it answers "gone". Everything is read with plain git in the project root; nothing is fetched or copied.
- **Merge commit:** the git host's pull request data gains a `mergeCommit` field, and skill-github asks `gh` for it.
- **In the tab:** it stays visible for a selected run, says which source it is showing, and marks committed and uncommitted changes differently. When the changes are gone it shows one line saying so.
- **Unchanged:** the `#` file picker keeps reading the project's own files.

Two gaps the plan records:
- If this machine hasn't fetched the merge commit yet, the tab shows "gone from this machine" until a later fetch brings it in.
- The Changes section has the same fallback-to-root bug. It's marked as a follow-up, or to be fixed in the same PR if that's cheap.

The ticket is not back on the queue for building, so someone needs to queue it before an agent will pick it up.
